title: The lights came out night three
body: Worth the long flight. The driver-guide knew exactly where to chase clear sky and we had a clean 40 minutes of dancing green ribbon over a black-sand beach. Hotel hot tubs facing the dark were also a major mood. Pack a real coat — Iceland is colder than it looks in photos.
photoPrompt: iPhone photo from inside a car at night, dashboard partially visible, windshield showing a faint green aurora ribbon over a dark Icelandic road, slightly blurry, authentic travel snapshot, no people

title: Glacier walk made the trip
body: Reykjavik was lovely but the day on the Vatnajökull ice cave is what I won't forget. Crampons, helmet, blue everywhere. Our guide had been climbing here for 14 years and knew which cave entrance the sun would hit just right. Bring sunglasses — the glare in there is no joke.
photoPrompt: iPhone photo of crampons and waterproof boots on blue glacier ice, helmet shadow visible at edge of frame, candid travel snapshot, square aspect

title: Long days, big rewards
body: The pace is intense — three big driving days back-to-back. If you're after a relax-by-the-fire trip this isn't it. But the things you see in those days, you'd never find on your own. The Blue Lagoon Premium at the end was the right call after that much driving.
photoPrompt: iPhone selfie style shot — two friends bundled in winter coats laughing in front of a frozen waterfall in Iceland, slightly off-center, real natural smile, soft daylight

title: Tea ceremony was the surprise hit
body: Booked this expecting the temples to be the highlight but it was the tea ceremony with master Naoko that I keep thinking about. Three hours, a tiny room, the most precise hand movements I've ever watched. We didn't speak the whole time. Magical. Also: book the kaiseki dinner two months ahead.
photoPrompt: Smartphone shot of a small black matcha bowl with bright green tea in a tatami room, hands of a tea master pouring water in background slightly out of focus, natural window light, candid, square aspect

title: Dawn at Fushimi Inari is unreal
body: Get there by 6:00 like the agent says. By 7:30 it's a different place — full of selfie sticks. Before 7 we walked the whole thousand gates almost alone. The orange light coming through wood is one of those things photos don't catch. Ryokan was lovely too, the cypress bath every evening was the best part of the trip.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot looking down a Fushimi Inari torii gate tunnel at dawn, soft pink light filtering through, one woman in pale kimono walking ahead, candid travel angle, slightly tilted

title: Lovely but pricey
body: Kyoto is expensive in spring. Everything was beautiful and the ryokan was top-tier, but we were a bit overwhelmed by costs of small extras. Pre-book the kaiseki dinner — totally worth the splurge. Also Arashiyama on day four was packed by 10am, go earlier.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV shot of feet in white tabi socks on tatami floor with sliding paper screens, soft morning light, slightly blurry, authentic ryokan moment

title: The water-camp was magical
body: Two nights inside the delta in a tent on stilts. No roads, no internet, hippos grunting at night. Mokoro at sunrise through the lilies — quietest experience of my life. The Linyanti night drive turned up two leopards and a porcupine. Pricey but I will never forget it.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV from inside a poling mokoro dugout canoe, looking forward across calm water with lilies, skipper's hat partially in frame at top, soft morning light, candid travel shot

title: Once-in-a-lifetime, plan accordingly
body: This is not a budget trip. But you genuinely don't see Botswana any other way. Three camps, three different ecosystems, the leopard count alone was worth it (we saw five in seven days). The light aircraft flights between camps were a bonus — the delta from above is otherworldly.
photoPrompt: Smartphone window shot from inside a small bush plane, propeller blade slightly visible, delta channels and islands below from above, candid travel snap

title: Positano lives up to the hype
body: Yes the road in from Naples is white-knuckle. Yes the steps to the hotel were a workout with luggage. But waking up on a cliff above that sea, with a cappuccino on a balcony that overhangs the village — worth every drop of sweat. The Capri boat day was the highlight.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a Positano hotel balcony at golden hour, cup of espresso on the railing with the cascading pastel houses below and sea visible, candid, slightly tilted, warm light

title: Romantic but exhausting
body: This trip is gorgeous but it is also stairs. So many stairs. If you have knees that complain, plan accordingly. The limoncello workshop with the Minori family was unexpectedly the best part — three hours of warm conversation, lemons everywhere, you leave with a bottle of your own.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV of hands holding a small bottle of limoncello and a lemon, blurred Italian seaside backdrop behind, natural daylight, candid travel moment

title: Crossing on day three
body: We had the wildebeest crossing on the third drive, which our guide said was lucky. The whole vehicle went silent for about thirty minutes. The Masai village visit afterwards was respectful and not staged — we paid the school directly. Camp food was honestly better than I expected.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV from open Land Cruiser safari vehicle, dust and wildebeest visible across the savannah, edge of vehicle frame at side, candid travel snap, square aspect

title: Balloon at dawn is the splurge to take
body: Skip something else if you must, do the balloon. Wake at 4am, basket fills, you drift over the herds. Champagne breakfast on landing under an acacia tree feels invented for a movie. Our guide Joseph also bird-id'd 60+ species — turns out the small birds are half the trip.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside hot-air balloon basket above African plains at sunrise, basket edge and ropes visible at bottom, golden light on the savannah below, candid travel angle

title: Heads-up: the drive in is long
body: Charter the flight from Wilson if you can — the road from Nairobi is a four-hour shake. Once at camp everything was great. Big-five list done by day three. Camp at night with lions roaring in the distance is something else. Bring warmer layers than you think — pre-dawn drives are cold.
photoPrompt: iPhone selfie of a couple in beige safari shirts under an acacia tree at golden hour, soft savannah light, candid, slightly off-center, real smiles

title: Three perfect days
body: Five nights was the right length. The Louvre after-hours was a small group, no lines, the guide Hugo knew every figure in every painting we passed. Marais apartment was tiny but exactly where you want to be. The market lunch at the apartment was the best meal of our trip.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of a Parisian café terrace from a sidewalk angle, two empty cane chairs and a small marble table with espressos and a half-eaten croissant, candid travel angle, soft afternoon light

title: Paris is Paris
body: Crowded as always. The after-hours Louvre and the Sunday market were the highlights. The bistro on rue Paul Bert lived up to its reputation — book a week ahead. Hotel was small but clean and the location is unbeatable.
photoPrompt: iPhone snap of a half-eaten pain au chocolat on a paper napkin on a metro seat, sunlight from window, candid commute moment in Paris

title: Japow is real
body: Niseko delivered. Three powder days in a row, knee-deep, the kind of skiing that ruins other ski trips for you. Two days with the back-country guide were worth it on top — the gates take you to whole hidden bowls. Onsen every evening, beer in the snow. I cried a little on the flight home.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of skis stuck upright in deep snow with Mount Yotei in the distance, soft pink alpine light, candid après-ski moment, no people

title: Sapporo ramen detour was worth it
body: We did the Sapporo day mid-week and ate at three ramen shops. Sumire's miso ramen is going to live in my dreams. The lodge in Niseko was beautiful — wooden, soft lights, hot tub on the deck under the snow. Pricey but you understand why.
photoPrompt: iPhone overhead shot of a steaming bowl of miso ramen with butter melting on top, chopsticks in hand at edge of frame, warm ramen-shop tungsten light, candid food photo

title: Two trips in one
body: Ngorongoro crater was unreal — you literally drop down into a wildlife colosseum. The moving Serengeti camp was the most luxurious tent I've slept in. Then four nights of doing nothing on Zanzibar with a beach villa twenty steps from the sand. Recommend doing safari first, beach second.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside a safari Land Cruiser pop-top roof, dust trail behind and acacia silhouette ahead, golden hour light, candid travel angle

title: Zanzibar should be 5 nights
body: Loved the safari but the Zanzibar finale was three nights and we wished for two more. Stone Town is worth a day. The spice farm tour is much better than it sounds — fresh nutmeg, cardamom, vanilla. Beach hotel was perfect. The dhow sunset cruise — book this.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of feet in sand on Zanzibar beach with traditional dhow sailboat on turquoise water in background, slightly tilted, golden hour, candid

title: Self-drive Aotearoa magic
body: Three weeks would still not be enough, but nine nights done well is plenty. The drive from Lake Tekapo to Mt Cook — words fail. Roy's Peak climb is brutal and worth it. Milford Sound on a clear day is a religious experience. We saved one hot-air helicopter day for Fiordland — best money we spent.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV from rental car driving across New Zealand's empty single-lane road with snow-capped peaks ahead, partial steering wheel visible at bottom, candid road-trip angle

title: Long way to go
body: Two flights and a transit each way. But once you're on the South Island, it's mind-bending how empty and beautiful it is. The Lake Wanaka tree at dawn is more crowded than the photos let on — go before sunrise. Glacier helicopter was the splurge highlight.
photoPrompt: iPhone selfie style shot of a couple in fleece jackets at Mt Cook viewpoint, mountains behind them slightly blurred, real candid smile, golden hour

title: The balloons are not a cliché
body: You see the photos for years and still it's somehow better in person. Dozens of balloons rising while you watch from a cave-hotel rooftop with tea. We did the flight on day two and walked through Love Valley on day four — both unforgettable. The cave bedroom is wild — vaulted stone, no windows, dead quiet.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a cave hotel rooftop terrace at sunrise — Turkish coffee cup in foreground, dozens of hot air balloons rising in the warm pink sky behind, candid composition, slightly off-center

title: Pottery class was unexpectedly fun
body: The balloon ride is what brings you here, but the pottery class in Avanos was a sleeper hit. The master's hands moved faster than ours could think. We came home with two slightly wonky bowls. The night-spot tour to Derinkuyu underground city felt indiana-jones.
photoPrompt: iPhone close-up of muddy hands at a pottery wheel shaping a vessel, terracotta clay everywhere, warm workshop light, candid hands-on photo

title: Two Balis in one week
body: The Ubud half was lush, jungle-y, hot. The Lembongan half was sea, hammocks, sleep. The contrast made each better. The manta point snorkel was incredible — we saw four mantas in fifteen minutes. Hire a scooter in Lembongan, the island is tiny.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of feet on a wooden over-water bungalow deck with turquoise lagoon below, manta ray faintly visible through clear water, candid travel angle

title: Watch the traffic
body: Ubud is heaven but the drive between airport and the villa took 2.5 hours of stop-and-go. Once we were up in the rice terraces though, paradise. The yoga at the Yoga Barn was crowded but lovely. Try the warungs — the cheap ones are better than the fancy places.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of a Balinese offering plate of frangipani flowers and incense on a stone step in the morning, candid temple moment, soft daylight

title: The rorbu cabin makes it
body: Sleeping on stilts over a fjord with snow outside and a fireplace inside is the picture of a Nordic dream. Aurora four out of seven nights. The trollfjord cruise in the winter was the kind of beauty that makes you stop talking. The cabin sauna at the end of long days was perfect.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV from inside a red rorbu cabin window looking out at a calm fjord with snow-covered cliffs and northern lights visible above, candle reflection in glass, candid moody travel shot

title: Cold but worth every layer
body: Pack heavier than you think — even the locals were in proper down. Aurora photography workshop was a highlight. The fish dinner in Henningsvær is a small detour and totally worth it. Long travel day getting there and back though, factor that in.
photoPrompt: iPhone selfie of a person in heavy parka with green northern lights ribbon over snow-covered peaks behind, blurry face, candid cold-cheek selfie

title: Three palaces, one camel, no regrets
body: Samode Haveli, the city palace in Jodhpur, then the Taj Lake Palace — each one a different fantasy. The Thar dune dinner was the dream we booked the trip for. Bring patience for the long road days — Indian distances are slow. And book Taj Lake Palace months ahead.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a moving rickshaw of a Jodhpur blue painted alley with women in saris walking, slight motion blur, candid travel angle, square aspect

title: Sensory overload in the best way
body: Nothing prepared me for how loud and colorful Jaipur is. The Amer fort on elephant-back at dawn felt regal, the bazaar at dusk was a blur of spice and motorbikes. Sleep was sometimes hard — courtyards echo at night. Hire the guide every day, you'll appreciate it.
photoPrompt: iPhone overhead shot of a thali plate with multiple small steel bowls of curries, naan in the corner, candid Indian food photo, warm restaurant light

title: Lake Louise canoe at sunrise
body: Get the first canoe rental of the morning — the lake is empty and the reflections are perfect. The Icefields Parkway is the most beautiful drive of my life. Helicopter onto the Columbia Icefield was unreal. Banff itself is touristy but the surrounding park makes up for it.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside red canoe on still turquoise water of Lake Louise at dawn, paddle visible at edge of frame, mountains reflected, candid sunrise paddling moment

title: Bear safety chat included
body: The ranger morning was great — saw a grizzly at 200 metres from a respectful distance. Lake Moraine was packed at 9am, go at 6. The Fairmont Chateau is expensive but you're paying for the location. The tea house hike to Lake Agnes is doable for any fitness level.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a wooden boardwalk in alpine meadow with distant grizzly silhouette, blurry due to telephoto reach, candid wildlife photo

title: Dahabiya cruise was the best part
body: Eight cabins, slow sailing, anchored at temples the cruise ships can't reach. The crew was warm, the food was excellent, the sunset on the upper deck with a gin and tonic — bookworthy. Abu Simbel is wild — book the dawn flight.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from the upper deck of a Nile dahabiya at sunset, two lateen sails silhouetted against orange sky, glass of wine on the railing, candid travel angle

title: Karnak temple complex is overwhelming
body: The Egyptologist guide was the difference between 'old stones' and 'I understand what I'm looking at'. Cairo traffic is intense. Stay at a hotel with a river view and a proper breakfast — you'll appreciate it after the long heat. Pack electrolytes.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot looking up between two massive Karnak hypostyle columns with hieroglyphs visible, dust beam of sunlight, candid travel angle, slightly tilted

title: Glass-floor bungalow makes you laugh
body: You look down and there are stingrays. You look up and there's Mount Otemanu. Breakfast comes by canoe. The lagoon snorkel with reef sharks was a hard yes — they ignore you. The private motu picnic with our chef Manu was the highlight of our honeymoon.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot looking down through clear glass floor in a Bora Bora bungalow at stingrays and tropical fish below, slightly distorted by water, candid travel moment

title: Long way, worth it
body: Three flights to get here from Europe. Once you're on the lagoon transfer though, the long travel evaporates. The resort is small — you see the same faces all week which is nice. Sunset cruise around Otemanu was magic.
photoPrompt: iPhone selfie of a couple on private overwater deck at sunset with mountain peak in the background, candid hugging selfie, soft warm light

title: Dawn at the Treasury — empty
body: Get in when the gate opens. You walk the kilometre of the Siq with maybe ten other people in front of you, and when the canyon opens onto the Treasury you can stand there alone for ten minutes. Petra by Night with the candles was magical. Wadi Rum tent under stars is unmatched.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside the narrow Siq canyon walking toward the pink Treasury facade just visible at the end, slightly blurry, candid early morning travel angle

title: Wadi Rum is Mars
body: Spent two nights in a Bedouin-style camp with a glass dome for stargazing. The 4x4 day through the canyons was a long bumpy ride but the rock arches and old Nabataean inscriptions are worth every bruise. Add a third night in Wadi Rum if you can.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot through a transparent dome ceiling of a Wadi Rum tent at night, Milky Way visible above the orange sand walls outside, candid stargazing angle

title: Helicopter sunrise was unreal
body: Skipped the line for the Statue of Liberty by doing the helicopter ride at dawn — the city was glowing gold. Broadway show was The Outsiders, my partner cried twice. The pastrami at Katz's lives up to every meme. Four nights felt exactly right.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside helicopter cabin with Manhattan skyline and Statue of Liberty visible through window at sunrise, propeller blade slightly visible, candid aerial travel moment

title: Crowded and worth it
body: You can't avoid the crowds in Times Square at peak times. But the after-hours Met was a small group of 20 — Egyptologist guide was great. The Brooklyn food tour on day three was a sleeper hit. We hit a jazz set at the Village Vanguard that I'll think about for a long time.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of warm New York deli interior with red banquettes and pastrami sandwich on rye in foreground on a paper-lined plate, candid food snapshot

title: Reykjavik food surprised me
body: Expected the wildlife and weather to be the headline. The Reykjavik food scene was unexpectedly excellent — the lamb at Matur og Drykkur, the seafood at Snaps. Hot springs in highlands were our quiet day favorite. Pack waterproof everything.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of a steaming Icelandic seafood soup in a stone-walled restaurant, candle on the table, soft warm light, candid food photo

title: Cherry blossom timing nailed it
body: Booked late, got the peak week by accident. Maruyama park was a dream and not nearly as crowded as the famous spots. Yanaka day in Tokyo before/after Kyoto is recommended. The kintsugi class with the gold-repair master was unexpectedly meditative.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of sakura cherry blossoms in foreground with a pagoda silhouetted in soft pink Kyoto evening light behind, candid travel angle, slightly tilted

title: Mokoro mornings forever
body: Two hours through the reeds with a polor who knew every bird call. Pure silence broken only by the occasional hippo grunt. You sit literally inches above the water. The walking safari from the camp was just as good — your guide reads tracks like a book.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV of feet in light pants inside a wooden mokoro canoe gliding through reeds, soft morning mist, candid water-level travel angle

title: The Capri private boat day made the trip
body: We've been on day-tripper boats to Capri before. Doing it from Positano on our own boat is a different thing entirely. Lunch at La Fontelina on the rocks, swim at the Faraglioni, the captain Salvatore knew every cave. €450 well spent.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a small wooden boat off Capri, the famous Faraglioni rock arches visible in soft afternoon light, edge of bow with white cushion visible, candid travel angle

title: Best wildlife photography of my life
body: Brought a telephoto for the first time. The Mara at sunset with backlit lion cubs — I'll never come close to that again. Guides know exactly where to position the vehicle for the light. Hot showers and three-course dinners in the tents felt surreal each evening.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of a long telephoto camera lens resting on a Land Cruiser door frame pointed at a distant lion silhouette on a kopje at golden hour, candid wildlife-photography moment

title: Perfume class was the unexpected hit
body: Three hours with a working nose, building our own scents from real ingredients. We left with bespoke perfumes. The Sunday market and home lunch was the perfect French day — fresh cheese, baguette, wine, balcony, sunshine. Five nights was just right.
photoPrompt: iPhone overhead shot of a Parisian market spread on a wooden apartment table with cheese plate, baguette, wine, and grapes, candid home meal photo

title: Worth the long flight
body: Three flights from Europe but the snow doesn't lie. The lodge had a private outdoor onsen on our deck and we used it every single night, often twice. The Sapporo ramen day was the perfect rest from the slopes. Came back craving Japan generally.
photoPrompt: iPhone steamy shot of person's shoulders in private outdoor onsen with cedar tub, snow falling lightly into the steaming water, candid relaxation moment, soft tungsten light

title: Spice farm tour with Suleiman
body: Skip the cheap tours, do the proper one with a local guide. Suleiman walked us through cardamom, vanilla, nutmeg and pepper. We bought enough to spice our cooking for a year. Stone Town carved doors are unreal — go with someone who can read the symbols.
photoPrompt: iPhone close-up of hands holding fresh nutmeg and cardamom pods on a banana leaf in Zanzibar spice farm, candid travel moment, soft daylight

title: Did the whole drive ourselves
body: Self-drive is the only way. Empty single-lane roads, sheep, Mt Cook out the window, music going. Routeburn track day hike was incredible. Milford Sound on a rainy day actually beats clear days — waterfalls everywhere. Save Queenstown for last, it's a perfect way to end.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV from a rental car driving along New Zealand single-lane road with sheep on hillsides and snow peaks ahead, partial dashboard visible, candid road-trip moment

title: Sunrise on the cave roof
body: Sleeping in a room carved into volcanic rock is the closest you'll get to time travel. We did the balloon on the second morning — the lift-off in the dark, the silent rise as the sky turns pink, the field of other balloons. Get a window seat at dinner — the view goes on.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a cave hotel terrace at sunrise of dozens of hot-air balloons rising, two coffee cups in the foreground, candid early morning composition

title: Sea kayak through Mangroves was bliss
body: Lembongan's mangrove channels at dawn — you can't believe it's the same world as Kuta. Manta point delivered on the snorkel side. Try the Locavore tasting menu in Ubud at least once. Travel light, hot the whole trip.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a kayak in Bali mangrove channel with green tunnels of roots, kayak nose visible at bottom of frame, candid morning paddle moment

title: Photography workshop was great
body: If you've never shot the northern lights, the camera settings are not intuitive. The night photographer in Reine gave us a two-hour crash course and our shots from the next nights were dramatic. Henningsvær on the chain bridge drive is a small Lofoten treasure.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of a camera on tripod with green aurora ribbon and starry sky behind, snow at the base, candid photographer's setup at night

title: Taj Lake Palace closed the deal
body: Two nights at the Taj Lake Palace was the slowing-down we needed after eight days of palaces and forts. Sunset boat back to the hotel feels like a movie. Don't skip the Chinchero weaver workshop in Jaipur — handwoven scarves are real, and reasonably priced.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of the Taj Lake Palace white marble hotel from a small wooden boat at dusk approaching, water rippling, candid arrival moment

title: Hot springs after long drives
body: The Banff Upper Hot Springs after the Icefields Parkway drive was perfect. Cave and Basin is touristy but quick. Skip Banff town restaurants and drive to Canmore for better food. Wildlife: black bear in our parking lot on day one, didn't expect that.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside steaming hot spring pool looking out at snow-dusted Canadian Rocky peaks, towel folded on edge in foreground, candid evening relax

title: Pyramids before opening time
body: Pre-dawn arrival at Giza was the right call — empty, soft light, no touts yet. The new Grand Egyptian Museum had only opened recently when we visited and they were still installing some galleries. Don't skip Abu Simbel — long day but unforgettable.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of the three pyramids of Giza at dawn with soft pink sky, no people, candid wide-angle travel snap

title: Pricey but it's the honeymoon
body: It costs what it costs. You pay for that lagoon. The reef snorkel was the highlight outside the resort itself. Food was fine but average for the price. Sunset on the deck made up for every annoyance. Bring a book — the wifi is intentionally weak.
photoPrompt: iPhone POV from end of overwater bungalow ladder looking down into clear turquoise lagoon water with coral visible, candid swim moment, soft light

title: Hot but worth every minute
body: October was still 30°C+. Bring electrolytes. The Monastery climb is steep (800 steps) but the reward is being mostly alone there. Wadi Rum 4x4 was bumpier than expected — sit in front if you have a bad back. Dead Sea float-day before flights was the perfect cooldown.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a Wadi Rum 4x4 ride looking forward at orange dunes and rock arches, partial vehicle frame and another tourist's bag visible at edge, candid bumpy ride moment

title: Smaller is better
body: Four nights in SoHo was perfect — far enough from Midtown chaos, close enough to walk to Greenwich Village. The food walk in Brooklyn day three was a sleeper hit. We didn't even feel the urge to do Times Square at all. Will come back.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from a SoHo cobblestone street with iron facade buildings and a yellow cab parked, soft afternoon light, candid New York street photo

title: Driver-guide system is the right call
body: We considered self-drive but the roads in winter were sketchy. Our driver-guide read weather constantly and rerouted us twice mid-day to chase clear sky. Three aurora nights, one massive snow detour. The Blue Lagoon on the last day after that intensity — chef's kiss.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from inside the Blue Lagoon spa with a person's hand holding a glass of champagne, steaming blue water and silica face mask visible, candid spa moment

title: Yanaka extension was unexpected highlight
body: We extended two nights in Tokyo's Yanaka after the Kyoto week. Old wooden buildings, slow neighbourhood, cats everywhere. If you're already going this far, add it. The ryokan in Higashiyama was the best part of the Kyoto stretch — book the higher tier with private bath.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot of a Tokyo Yanaka old wooden alley with a black cat sitting on a stone wall and a paper lantern, soft afternoon light, candid neighbourhood moment

title: Ravello over Positano for a slow day
body: Positano is the iconic photo. Ravello is where you actually relax. Villa Cimbrone gardens with the infinity terrace, long lunch at Belmond Caruso. We did Ravello on day four after two intense Capri/Positano days and it was the right pacing.
photoPrompt: iPhone shot from Villa Cimbrone infinity terrace in Ravello with Mediterranean below and two empty marble busts on stone pillars in the foreground, candid scenic moment
